channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: Indian Rupee: Range-bound trade risks around CPI – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale strategists note that India’s June Consumer Price Index (CPI) release will be important for bond markets, with the 10-year IGB yield holding near its 200-day moving average around 6.71%.

item.title: British Pound: Gilt confidence and new leadership – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu argues that United Kingdom (UK) assets, including the British Pound (GBP) and gilts, will react more to the choice of chancellor under incoming Prime Minister Andy Burnham than to the leadership change itself.

item.title: AUD/USD Price Forecast: Wavers around 0.6950 with bearish momentum fading
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) posts marginal losses against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday, as the pair's reversal from Friday's 0.6970 highs found support above 0.6120. Rising tensions in Iran have hammered risk appetite, but the US Dollar’s weakness is keeping the Aussie from retreating further.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Monday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $58.72 per troy ounce, down 1.92% from the $59.87 it cost on Friday.

item.title: Oil: Markets price renewed Hormuz risks – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank strategist Michael Every discusses rising geopolitical risks around the Strait of Hormuz after the apparent collapse of a US-Iran memorandum of understanding. Every notes both sides are now striking each other, with United States (US) strategy shifting to escorted energy flows.

item.title: Indian Rupee resumes upside amid surging Oil prices
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades significantly lower against the US Dollar (USD) on Monday. The USD/INR jumps to over a six-week high around 95.95, as renewed Middle East hostilities have strengthened oil prices.

item.title: US Dollar: Higher energy supports Fed tightening – ING
item.description: ING analysts Chris Turner, Frantisek Taborsky and Francesco Pesole note that higher energy prices and tensions in the Gulf are supporting the Dollar against low-yielding currencies. They highlight that US energy independence and live Fed tightening prospects underpin Dollar strength.

item.title: Euro recovers early losses against Canadian Dollar, BoC policy eyed
item.description: The Euro (EUR) claws back its early losses and turns slightly positive at around 1.6170 against the Canadian Dollar (CAD) during the European trading session on Monday. The cross bounces back as the Euro strengthens amid hopes that the ongoing aggression in the Middle East won’t be prolonged.

item.title: EUR/USD Price Forecast: Rises to near 1.1450 after breaking above nine-day EMA
item.description: EUR/USD gains ground after posting losses in the previous day, trading around 1.1440 during the European hours on Monday. The currency pair holds just above the nine-day Exponential Moving Average (EMA) but remains capped by the 50-day EMA, keeping the near-term tone cautiously bearish.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Mixed outlook within defined band against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that USD/JPY rebounded after a sharp drop to 161.26, with intraday gains expected to be capped between 161.60 and 162.45. Over the next 1–3 weeks, the outlook is described as mixed, with trading likely between 160.60 and 163.00.

item.title: United States Dollar Index Price Forecast: Bears await break below 23.6% Fibo. near 100.80
item.description: The US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback against a basket of currencies, attracts some sellers following an intraday uptick to the 101.22 area on Monday and fills a modest weekly bullish gap.

item.title: Iran confirms Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan continue to mediate with US
item.description: A spokesperson from the Iranian Foreign Ministry has confirmed in the European trade on Monday that efforts from Qatar, Oman, and Pakistan to mediate tensions with the United States (US) continue.

item.title: Brent: Rebound tests key resistance – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale’s Kenneth Broux notes that Brent has sharply rebounded after defending the late-February low around $69 and is now testing the 200-day moving average and a descending trendline.

item.title: Gold pares intraday losses; keeps the red below $4,100 amid hawkish Fed expectations
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) trims a part of its intraday losses during the first half of the European session on Monday, though it retains the negative bias for the second straight day and remains below the $4,100 mark. The US Dollar (USD) attracts some intraday sellers and supports the bullion.

item.title: USD/CHF Price Forecast: Bulls remain capped below 0.8100 despite the risk-off market
item.description: The US Dollar posts moderate gains against the Swiss Franc (CHF) on Monday, yet with price action contained within the last two weeks’ trading range, and with the 0.8100 level capping bulls for now.

item.title: Turkish Lira: Policy limits keep TRY under pressure – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose contrasts upbeat remarks from CBT governor Fatih Karahan with more cautious comments from deputy governor Gazi Ishak Kara on Turkey’s inflation dynamics.

item.title: Dow Jones futures slip on rising risk aversion
item.description: Dow Jones futures lose 0.12% to trade around 52,840 during European trading hours on Monday. Meanwhile, S&P 500 futures and Nasdaq 100 futures fall 0.45% and 1.30%, trading near 7,580 and 29,640, respectively.

item.title: Euro gains strongly against Japanese Yen as latter underperforms across board
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is higher by 0.36% to near 185.25 against the Japanese Yen (JPY) during the European trading session on Monday. The Japanese Yen underperforms across the board despite hopes that Japan’s inflation would remain above the Bank of Japan’s (BoJ) 2% target for a longer period.

item.title: Equities: Earnings and Fed signals in focus – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank strategists highlight that the S&P 500 closed at 7575, gaining 0.42%, after a strong week supported by stabilising chip stocks and a rebound in the Philly semiconductor index.

item.title: Japanese Yen sticks to losses vs USD as bears shrug off intervention fears amid Iran risks
item.description: The USD/JPY pair sticks to its modest intraday gains through the early European session on Monday and currently trades above the 162.00 mark, up 0.30% for the day.

item.title: WTI Oil holds below $75.00 despite the deteriorating Middle East conflict
item.description: Speculative traders seem reluctant to jump on the Crude Oil rally despite the escalating tensions in the Middle East and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Intervention risks rise again – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner highlights that USD/JPY is grinding higher above 162 as higher energy prices pressure Asian currencies. He notes that Japanese authorities may follow a similar intervention pattern to last year, with potential action ahead of the Marine Day holiday.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD falls to near $58.00 due to prevailing bearish bias
item.description: XAG/USD struggles for the second consecutive day, trading around $58.20 per troy ounce during the European hours on Monday. The technical analysis of the daily chart shows that the spot price is remaining within the descending channel pattern, suggesting a prevailing bearish bias.

item.title: British Pound: Rally fades into range trade against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that GBP/USD gapped lower after briefly breaking above 1.3445, with momentum turning down and risks of a test below 1.3360, though 1.3320 is seen as distant for now.

item.title: US Dollar: Modest grind higher with CPI in focus – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong expect the US Dollar (USD) to appreciate by around 2–3% by end-2026, supported versus low-yielding currencies such as the Euro (EUR) and Swiss Franc (CHF).

item.title: EUR/GBP Price Forecast: Steadies near 0.8500 with upside attempts limited
item.description: The Euro (EUR) is trading practically flat against the British Pound (GBP) on Monday after dropping about 2% over the past three weeks. Euro bulls remain subdued amid the risk-averse mood, but sellers are struggling to find acceptance below 0.8500.

item.title: British Pound remains subdued as US-Iran tensions lift US Dollar
item.description: GBP/USD remains in negative territory after paring daily losses, trading around 1.3390 during the early European hours on Monday. The pair faces challenges as the US Dollar (USD) gains ground on rising safe-haven demand amid intensifying tensions in the Middle East.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Higher Oil prices strengthen Canadian Dollar
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) trades firmly against its major currency peers, but is flat at around 1.4160 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Monday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar holds steady near 0.5750 as US launches new wave of strikes against Iran
item.description: The NZD/USD pair trades on a flat note near 0.5760 during the early European trading hours on Monday. Escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East following the US's launch of fresh missile attacks against Iran on Sunday boost the US Dollar (USD) as a safe-haven asset.

item.title: Brent: Geopolitics lift prices as speculators stay cautious – ING
item.description: ING analysts Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that Brent Oil prices have risen sharply as tensions escalate in the Persian Gulf and transit through the Strait of Hormuz slows. They highlight that speculators have trimmed net long positions in ICE Brent despite higher prices.
